sections.title: Your point of view
sections.description: Select walking, cycling, or both. Questions will adapt to your selection.

questions.text: How do you move through this place? You can choose both answers.

options.text: Person walking or rolling (also with a stroller, cane, walker or wheelchair)
Person cycling or riding an e-scooter

options.text: Going to or from a bus, tram or metro stop

sections.title: Quick assessment
sections.description: Answer these first. Then you can finish or add optional details.

questions.text: What kind of crossing or passage is this?
questions.help: A passage is any way to get across a road, a railway or a difference in level.

options.text: A street crossing (zebra crossing or intersection)
A bridge or footbridge over the road
An elevator, an escalator, a ramp or a few steps between two levels (a longer stairway is assessed as a street segment)

questions.text: How is this crossing controlled?

options.text: Zebra crossing without a traffic light
No zebra stripes and no traffic light

questions.text: Who is this crossing for?

options.text: There are separate markings for bicycles next to the pedestrian ones
Not marked for bicycles, but bicycles use it

questions.text: Which best describes using this place on foot?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little
I need to be careful while passing
It takes a lot of effort or attention
I avoid using it if possible
I cannot get through (for example with a wheelchair or stroller)

questions.text: Because of traffic (cars, motorcycles, bicycles), how risky does it feel to use this place on foot?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little

It takes a lot of effort or attention

questions.help: Harassment means unwanted comments, gestures or contact. This question is about your own feeling, not about traffic.

options.text: I do not go there in the evening

questions.text: How does this crossing work?
questions.help: Turning cars are vehicles that turn at the junction and drive across the crossing while the light for people crossing is green. Who should go refers to the right of way, that is who is allowed to go first.

Zebra crossing without a traffic light

sections.title: Access and crossing
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: Can people on foot use this place?

options.text: Yes, but not with a wheelchair or stroller
Yes, but it is hard to understand where to go
No, it is closed or forbidden
No, it is not possible to get through

options.text: Yes, with a dedicated bicycle space
Yes, but you need to get off and push the bicycle
No, it is not possible to get through by bicycle or e-scooter

questions.text: By bicycle or e-scooter, what problems do you find at this crossing?

options.text: The cycle path stops before or after the crossing
There is no crossing for bicycles: people use the zebra crossing
Cars do not give way to bicycles

options.text: No, the escalator is broken or stopped

questions.text: How do you get the green light to cross?

options.text: It comes by itself, every cycle
You have to press the button, and it works
There is a button, but it does not work

options.text: Yes, but it does not work or can barely be heard

questions.text: How many traffic lanes must people cross here?

What blocks the view?

options.text: Parked or stopped cars or vans
Signs, poles, boxes, or street furniture

questions.text: Can people clearly see the path and the exit?

options.text: Yes, the path and exit are clearly visible
No, there are blind corners or hidden areas

sections.title: Orientation and space
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: How easy is it to understand where people should go?
Why is it difficult to understand?

options.text: The crossing or passage is hard to recognize
It is not clear if people can walk here
It is not clear if people can cycle here

questions.text: Is there enough safe space to wait before crossing or to stop and rest?

options.text: A place exists, but it is too small
No space to wait or rest is needed here

questions.text: Who might find it hard or impossible to use this place?

options.text: People using a walker or walking aid
Children (for example walking alone to school)
People who walk slowly or need more time (for example older people)
People who find it hard to find their way or understand signs

sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: What helps people use this place safely?

sections.description: Tell us whether improving this place should be a priority.
